candidate.claim: Under correlated/common-random-number simulation sampling, allocation based on covariance of candidate differences can improve probability of correct selection and simulation efficiency relative to equal or independence-derived allocation in the paper's finite-design examples.

primary_source.title: Optimal Computing Budget Allocation Under Correlated Sampling
primary_source.venue: Proceedings of the 2004 Winter Simulation Conference

problem_and_method.objective: Allocate a fixed simulation-replication budget among a finite set of designs to maximize probability of correct selection (PCS) when design samples are correlated.
problem_and_method.two_design_result: The paper derives the exact continuous optimum for two correlated Gaussian designs. Let c=sigma1/sigma2 >=1; if 2*rho >= c - 1/c, equal allocation N1=N2=T/2 is optimal. Thus sufficiently high positive correlation relative to variance imbalance can make equal allocation optimal rather than requiring stronger skew.
problem_and_method.multi_design_result: For more than two designs the paper proposes an approximate Correlated Budget Allocation (CBA) procedure using estimated means/covariances; the correlated allocation depends on variances, mean gaps and correlations with the current best design.

numerical_protocol.precision_claim: approximately three decimal places for estimated PCS
numerical_protocol.parenthetical_budget_semantics: For the Gaussian examples, parentheses report the total EBA sampling budget required to reach the PCS achieved by CBA at T=500. In the queue table the accompanying text analogously states EBA needs >2x the budget to match CBA PCS and >3x to match sequential CBA PCS.

equal_variance_example.scope_note: At very high positive correlation CBA coincides with EBA in this example, consistent with the analytic equal-allocation boundary.

UU1_queue_example.setup: Single-server FCFS U/U/1 queue, 10 designs; interarrival U(4,14), design-dependent service U(1,15.5+0.5i); performance is negative expected average system time over first 15 customers; CRN uses the same arrival process with independent service times.
UU1_queue_example.sequential_detail: seqCBA starts with n0 and allocates the remaining budget incrementally in batches of 20 in this example instead of one two-stage allocation.

scope_clarifications: The strong numeric savings are example-specific finite-design simulation results, not a universal factor for semantic LLM/agent evaluation.

The derivation is primarily Gaussian correlated sampling; the paper only summarizes extensions to certain non-Gaussian settings under additional moment-generating-function/copula conditions. Do not label the main allocation formula distribution-free.

The paper's correlated-sampling setting is common-random-number simulation where paired covariance is estimable. Transferring this to shared LLM benchmark seeds/scenarios is a hypothesis that requires verifying that pairing induces stable useful covariance in the target metric.

Positive correlation is not a monotone instruction to skew allocation more aggressively. At sufficiently high positive correlation relative to variance imbalance, equal allocation is analytically optimal for two designs and empirically coincides with CBA in the rho=0.9 examples.

The paper states positive correlation improved simulation efficiency and negative correlation harmed it in the tested Gaussian examples. Therefore shared scenarios should not be assumed beneficial when they induce negative or unstable correlation.

Early covariance estimates are themselves noisy. The source algorithm estimates means/covariances from initial samples and sequential CBA can update allocation; the worker's recommendation to delay aggressive skew until covariance stabilizes is a reasonable transfer guardrail, not a separately measured paper result.
confidence: high for source-domain equations and numerical tables; medium only for transfer to stochastic agent/research evaluation
unresolved: Direct agent-evaluation experiment comparing shared-seed covariance-aware replication allocation with independent/equal allocation at matched total evaluator cost.
Robust covariance-aware allocation under heavy-tailed or strongly non-Gaussian semantic scores without the paper's additional distributional conditions.
Finite-sample guardrails for noisy covariance estimation and misidentified current-best candidates in LLM evaluation.
downstream_instruction: Retain as source-domain evidence for covariance-aware common-scenario evaluation allocation. Keep transfer_hypothesis explicitly separate from verified simulation result; do not claim a universal 2-3x agent-evaluation speedup or that stronger positive correlation always warrants more unequal allocation.
